senses.definition: having good things happen to you by chance
senses.example: You were lucky to find a seat on such a busy train.

senses.definition: happening by chance and having a good result
senses.example: It was only a lucky guess, but I got the answer right.

senses.definition: believed to bring good fortune or success
senses.example: My grandfather always wore his lucky hat to football matches.

senses.definition: a container made of paper, plastic, cloth or leather, used for carrying things
senses.example: Don't forget to pack your bags before the taxi arrives.

senses.definition: dark areas of loose skin under a person's eyes
senses.example: After a week of late nights, I've got huge bags under my eyes.

senses.definition: a large amount or number of something
senses.example: Don't worry, there's bags of time before the film starts.

senses.definition: an unpleasant or unattractive older woman
senses.example: The neighbours called her a miserable old bag behind her back.

senses.definition: an activity or subject that someone likes or is good at
senses.example: Team sports were never really my bag.

grammar.note: usually in the negative, with a possessive

senses.definition: to put things into a bag
senses.example: The assistant bagged our groceries while we paid.

senses.definition: to manage to get something, often before other people can
senses.example: Get there early and bag us some good seats.

senses.definition: to catch or kill an animal when hunting
senses.example: The hunters bagged three ducks before lunch.

senses.definition: the power to give orders and make people obey them
senses.example: The authorities have closed the road after the flood.

senses.definition: an official organization or group with power to make decisions in an area
senses.example: Teachers need enough authority to keep order in class.

senses.definition: official permission or the right to do something
senses.example: Only the manager has the authority to sign these contracts.

senses.definition: a person with special knowledge of a subject whose opinion is respected
senses.example: She is a leading authority on medieval history.

senses.definition: the quality of making people respect and believe you through knowledge or confidence
senses.example: He spoke with such authority that nobody questioned him.

senses.definition: the ability to stay steady and upright without falling
senses.example: She slipped on the ice and lost her balance.

senses.definition: a state in which different things have the right amount or importance
senses.example: It's hard to find a good balance between work and family.

senses.definition: the amount of money in a bank account at a particular time
senses.example: I check my balance online before I go shopping.

senses.definition: the amount of money still owed after part has been paid
senses.example: You pay a deposit now and the balance next month.

senses.definition: an instrument for weighing things, with two dishes hanging from a bar
senses.example: The chemist placed the powder carefully on the balance.

senses.definition: to stay or keep something steady without it falling
senses.example: The waiter balanced three plates on one arm.

senses.definition: to give two or more things equal or fair importance
senses.example: Many parents struggle to balance their jobs and their children.

senses.definition: to make the money spent equal to the money received
senses.example: The government has promised to balance the budget by next year.

senses.definition: a person, team or animal that comes first in a competition, race or game
senses.example: The winners will be announced at the end of the evening.

senses.definition: something or someone that is successful or likely to be successful
senses.example: Your new recipe is a real winner with the kids.

senses.definition: a goal or point that makes a team or player win a game
senses.example: He scored the winner in the last minute of the match.

senses.definition: to move along a surface by turning over and over, or make something do this
senses.example: He rolled onto his back and looked up at the stars.

senses.definition: to turn your body over so that you lie in a different position
senses.example: The ball rolled slowly across the floor and under the sofa.

senses.definition: to move along smoothly on wheels, or make something do this
senses.example: The car started to roll backwards down the slope.

senses.definition: to move or flow smoothly and steadily in one direction
senses.example: Tears were rolling down her cheeks as she read the letter.

senses.definition: to turn something over and over to make it into a ball or tube shape
senses.example: Can you help me roll the carpet before the movers arrive?

senses.definition: to make something flat by pushing a round object over it
senses.example: Roll the dough until it is about half a centimetre thick.

senses.definition: to throw dice onto a surface in a game
senses.example: It's your turn, so roll the dice and move your piece.

senses.definition: to move your eyes upwards and around to show you are annoyed or bored
senses.example: My sister always rolls her eyes when I tell that joke.

senses.definition: to make a long, deep, continuous sound
senses.example: Thunder rolled in the distance as we hurried home.

senses.definition: a long piece of paper, cloth, film or other material turned around itself into a tube
senses.example: We need to buy another roll of toilet paper.

senses.definition: a small round loaf of bread for one person
senses.example: She had a cheese roll and an apple for lunch.

senses.definition: an official list of names of people belonging to a group
senses.example: The teacher calls the roll at the start of every class.

senses.definition: a single throw of dice in a game
senses.example: Everything depends on the next roll of the dice.

senses.definition: a long, deep, continuous sound
senses.example: A low roll of thunder came from the hills.

senses.definition: a movement in which a body turns over completely on the ground
senses.example: The children practised forward rolls on the gym mat.

relations.why: sounds the same as role, the part someone plays

senses.definition: to make a formal, usually written, request for something
senses.example: She has applied for a job at the local hospital.

senses.definition: to be relevant to someone or something and have an effect on them
senses.example: These rules apply to all students, including part-time ones.

senses.definition: to use a method, rule or knowledge in a particular situation
senses.example: We can apply this method to other problems as well.

senses.definition: to put or spread a substance on a surface
senses.example: Apply the cream to your skin twice a day.

senses.definition: to press or push on something with force
senses.example: Apply firm pressure to the wound to stop the bleeding.

senses.definition: to work hard and give all your attention to something
senses.example: If you apply yourself, you could pass every exam this year.

grammar.note: used with a reflexive pronoun: apply yourself

senses.definition: the number of points or goals each player or team has in a game
senses.example: The final score was three goals to one.

senses.definition: the number of marks or points someone gets in a test or exam
senses.example: Her test scores have improved a lot this term.

senses.definition: the written music for a piece, or the music written for a film or play
senses.example: The film's score was written by a famous composer.

senses.definition: a very large number of people or things
senses.example: Scores of people were waiting outside the stadium.

senses.definition: a group or set of twenty
senses.example: The old man had lived for four score years.

grammar.note: plural is usually score after a number: three score

senses.definition: to win a point or goal in a game or sport
senses.example: He scored twice in the second half of the match.

senses.definition: to get a particular number of marks or points in a test
senses.example: Most students scored above eighty per cent on the exam.

senses.definition: to achieve a success or gain an advantage
senses.example: The new album has scored a huge hit with teenagers.

senses.definition: to manage to get something you want, often by luck
senses.example: I scored two free tickets to tonight's concert.

senses.definition: to cut a line or lines into the surface of something
senses.example: Score the bread dough lightly with a sharp knife.

senses.definition: to write music for a film, play or group of instruments
senses.example: She was asked to score a new documentary about the ocean.
